result.title: Medical Image Segmentation Is Now Just Another Coding Task
result.summary: For decades, every new medical image segmentation task has needed an expert, a dedicated architecture, and a framework such as nnU-Net. This is no longer the case: medical image segmentation is now just another coding task. Given only a task description, labeled data, and a CPU (with no segmentation framework, no pretrained weights, and no human in the loop), four off-the-shelf coding agents built segmenters for 13 tasks across four imaging modalities within hours, an ability that has emerged rather than been built. On the nine 2D tasks, their best programs reach 99% of the Dice of a GPU-trained nnU-Net. Like any code, a segmenter improves by being revised and checked, so we ask how far the same agents can improve their own segmentations and what unlocks further gains. On unseen cases there is no reference, so the agents inspect renderings of their own predictions: this alone lifts the worst tenth of cases by 0.09 Dice and cuts boundary error (HD95) by almost a quarter. Far more is within reach. Told the true Dice of each attempt, the same agents improve in all 14 matched pairs, rescue 85% of failed masks instead of 30%, and surpass the GPU-trained nnU-Net on average, by producing better masks rather than by choosing among them. What unlocks these gains is a quality signal, which neither visual inspection, nor more rounds, nor a quality estimator trained by the agents themselves yet supplies: we call this the quality blind spot. The ability to build and to repair is already present; the next advance will come not from another segmentation model, but from reference-free quality estimation that coding agents can call.

AI.brief_summary: 论文展示四个现成编码代理仅凭任务描述、标注数据和 CPU 就能为 13 个医学分割任务自动编写分割程序，并进一步研究代理能否通过检查自身预测的渲染图来修订分割；结果显示真正的瓶颈是缺少无参考的质量信号，并称之为「quality blind spot」。
AI.relevance_reason: 「无参考质量估计」作为代理自我修订、判断是否继续改进的决策信号，可能与 LVR 中自验证、视觉证据筛选及停止/计算分配问题存在概念联系，可供核查；但研究对象是代码生成的分割流水线而非 latent 推理状态，联系仅为启发层面。
